issues.description: The problem specification (UML and textual description) declares checkOrderReady() as a parameterless method (checkOrderReady(): void), but the solution implementation declares checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This parameter mismatch means students following the specification would implement a parameterless method, while the provided solution uses an extra boolean parameter and calls checkOrderReady(true) from orderMeal. This divergence can confuse students about the correct method signature and cause incompatibility with automated tests or graders expecting the parameterless method.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution to match the specification: declare checkOrderReady() with no parameters (public void checkOrderReady()) and update orderMeal to call checkOrderReady() (without arguments). If logging is needed for debugging, use an internal flag or a separate private helper rather than changing the public signature.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) with a boolean parameter. This difference in the method signature creates an API mismatch: students implementing checkOrderReady() as required by the exercise will find a different method shape in the reference solution, which can cause confusion when mapping requirements to the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution API match the problem specification by providing a no-argument checkOrderReady() method. Either remove the boolean parameter from the existing method and call it without arguments from orderMeal, or add an overload public void checkOrderReady() that delegates to the parameterized implementation (or handles logging internally). This ensures the reference implementation uses the same method signature described in the problem.

issues.description: The problem title refers to 'Panic at Seal Saloon' while the repositories' project names in settings.gradle use 'Panic-at-Burger-House' and 'Panic-at-Burger-House-Solution'. The differing project names across problem statement, template, and solution may create minor confusion about the intended exercise target and identity.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the project naming across artifacts. Either update the template and solution settings.gradle rootProject.name values to match the problem statement ('H02E02 - Panic at Seal Saloon') or revise the problem statement title to reflect the repository project name. Consistent naming will reduce incidental confusion for students.
